answer: The tide miller grinds only when the tide turns, and chalks the sacks as the wheel slows, because flour ground on a false tide is flour short in the sack. Millwright apprenticeship record with guild attestation is the tide table's authority: four-year apprenticeship, 8,000 supervised hours, guild exam, annual dues. A sack ground under a false beacon comes up short when the flour is weighed, and the shortfall names the cheat. The jade is the forfeit, a month's grinding fees handed to the parish, while the umber is the tide book, kept beside the wheel and read at every audit.
